node-1.label: Rough sandpapery skin changes on the face present for 2½ years

node-2.label: A woman in her 70s with a history of polycythemia vera and acute myelogenous leukemia; the skin condition began before the AML diagnosis and hydroxyurea treatment.

node-3.label: The skin changes involved a rough sandpapery sensation without pruritus or pain, extending to the neck, upper chest, and bilateral forearms.

node-4.label: Physical examination showed background erythema with numerous rough horny spicules at the follicular ostia on the face, ears, neck, upper chest, and bilateral forearms, plus a pigmented macule on the right cheek.

node-5.label: Previous treatments with triamcinolone acetonide cream 0.1%, bacitracin ointment, and combination antibiotic ointment (neomycin sulfate, polymyxin B, and bacitracin) showed no improvement; daily medications included donepezil hydrochloride, melatonin, and aspirin 81 mg.
